concerns.text: The plan assumes the existence of publicly‑available battery cycling datasets with voltage, current, temperature, and capacity measurements (see the Summary and FR‑001 mapping). However, the accompanying research.md documents that no such open datasets are currently available and that a synthetic placeholder will be used. This mismatch means the core construct (real battery time‑series) is not measured, breaking construct validity and rendering the primary research question (“which early‑cycle signatures drive degradation”) unanswerable with the planned analysis.

Performance goals (≤ 6 h, ≤ 7 GB RAM) and the hyper‑parameter sweep are calibrated on a placeholder CSV that lacks the multi‑channel time‑series structure of real battery data. Consequently, the power analysis (N ≈ 1 000 rows) cited in research.md does not reflect the true sample‑size requirements for detecting a ΔR² = 0.05 in realistic battery datasets, risking under‑powered inference.

The protocol‑agnostic validation (SC‑004) relies on holding out entire protocol types, but the placeholder dataset contains no genuine protocol variation. Without real protocol heterogeneity, the held‑out test cannot assess generalization, so the confound control claim is unsupported.
